title: Band-9 Samples: What type of photos do you like taking? [Why/Why not?]
content:
This post contains ideas and band-9 sample answers (audio included) for the Cambridge IELTS 11 Academic Speaking Part 1 Question 1 Test 3 question:

“What type of photos do you like taking? [Why/Why not?]”

Sample 1

I absolutely love taking selfies, but not for the reasons you might think. It’s not about vanity for me, but rather a form of self-documentation. I find it interesting to look back on how I’ve grown and changed over time, both physically and emotionally. Seeing a visual timeline of my life helps me reflect on my personal journey and appreciate the person I’ve become.

Sample 2

I’m an avid traveler, and I enjoy capturing the essence of the places I visit through my photographs. They serve as a tangible memory of my journeys, encapsulating the cultures I’ve experienced, the people I’ve met, and the landscapes I’ve admired. While some people might argue it’s better to fully immerse in the moment rather than view it through a lens, I believe photography adds a creative dimension to my travels, making them even more rewarding.

Sample 3

I love capturing images of my meals and the eateries I frequent because it’s a way of sharing my love for food with others. I believe that food is more than just sustenance; it’s a form of sharing and caring. By posting these images on social media, I hope to encourage others to explore new cuisines and enjoy the pleasure of good food.

Sample 4

I’m very much into taking family photographs. They are more than just images to me; they are tangible memories that capture the essence of our relationships. Be it the laughter-filled family gatherings or the quiet moments of everyday life, these photographs are treasures that serve as a visual narrative of our shared journey. They remind us of the love, warmth, and togetherness that form the foundation of our family.

Sample 5

I must admit, I do enjoy taking photos of myself for social media. As an avid user of these platforms, I find it invigorating to share slices of my life with others. Posting these images and seeing the positive responses actually acts like a mood-lifter for me, making me feel more self-assured and content.

Sample 6

You know, I absolutely adore taking candid pictures. There’s something uniquely captivating about capturing people in their most authentic moments, when they’re oblivious to the camera. It’s like freezing a slice of reality that’s raw and untarnished. I mean, there’s a stark difference between posed pictures and candid ones, right? The former often feels contrived, while the latter exudes genuineness. It’s this organic nature of candid photos that really draws me toward them.

Sample 7

Abstract photography is my cup of tea. It’s all about breaking away from traditional rules and delving into the realm of creativity and imagination. I love how it challenges me to see ordinary objects from a completely different perspective. It’s about finding beauty in places where others might not see it, and that’s the whole thrill of it for me.

Sample 8

I find myself consistently drawn to capturing natural landscapes when I have my camera in hand. They offer a unique sense of peace that’s hard to find in my daily city life. It’s like a brief respite from the incessant noise and restlessness. When I look at the photos, I feel like I’m transported to a world that’s far removed from the stress and strain of my everyday life.

Sample 9

I have a penchant for clicking photos of everything around me, no matter how mundane it may seem. The magic lies in the ability to transform the ordinary into something extraordinary. A simple cup of coffee, a weathered door, or even a random street corner, each has its own charm if you capture it right.

Sample 10

To be frank, I’m not a huge aficionado of capturing images. The rationale behind this is my preference for minimalism. I lean towards experiencing moments first-hand rather than obsessing over recording them. For me, life is about cherishing the present, not storing it away in digital format.
